primitives.name: Signal System Coordination
primitives.verbatim_quote: I think this is a very useful feature of any good signal system.
primitives.assumptions: Signals must be discrete, learnable, and uniformly understood across team members.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When signal ambiguity exceeds threshold of interpretability.

layer2.mapping: Signal decoding in GSI mirrors play execution in GSE via shared information structure.

primitives.name: Repetitive Play Perfection
primitives.verbatim_quote: With signals come the beginnings of a team's repertory of plays, which, like the signals themselves, have to be learned by patient repetition until each man's place and part in each play is instinctive with him and thoroughly familiar to every other member of the team.
primitives.assumptions: Learning is deterministic over time; repetition leads to internalized action patterns.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When repetition fails to achieve instinctive behavior.

layer2.mapping: GSE state transition kernel derived from repetitive play training in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Individual and team performance metrics post-repetition cycles.

primitives.name: Sequential Play Learning
primitives.verbatim_quote: Nothing has ever been gained by trying to teach more than one play at once, and it is time wasted to overload a green eleven with any play which it does not immediately proceed to perfect.
primitives.assumptions: Parallel learning degrades performance; single-play mastery is optimal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When multiple play instruction exceeds cognitive load capacity.

layer2.mapping: GSI sequential learning aligns with GSE incremental play adoption.
layer2.telemetry: Performance degradation vs. number of concurrently taught plays.
